sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Manual snapshot capture job
sections.what: Starts only when someone presses Run by hand on the GitHub Actions page. It sets up a clean Linux machine, installs Playwright and Chromium, runs the snapshot script, and saves the new images to the repository only if any of them changed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the snapshot images are made by a script, so this job automates that step. The reason for manual-only start is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: It pushes straight to whichever branch it was started on, with no review step, so starting it from a branch other than main leaves the new images there.

summary: A manual job that makes fresh paper snapshot images and saves them back into the repository when they have changed.
purpose: Keep the saved snapshot images in public/media/snapshots up to date without someone running the capture by hand.
why: Likely reason: the snapshots come from a script, so this job automates regenerating them. Reason for manual-only start not stated in the code.
how: Starts from the GitHub Actions page. Sets up a clean Linux machine and Node.js 20. Installs Playwright version 1.56.1 without recording it in the project's package file, and installs headless Chromium. Runs scripts/capture-snapshots.mjs. Sets a bot identity for git, adds public/media/snapshots, and stops with a success message if nothing changed. Otherwise it commits and pushes.
inputs: A person pressing Run on the workflow page. The repository code, including scripts/capture-snapshots.mjs, which is not in the packet.
outputs: Updated images in public/media/snapshots and a new commit on the branch the run started from, only when images changed.
risks: It pushes straight to the branch it ran on, with write permission and no review step. Only the snapshot folder is added, so any other files the script writes are not saved. The capture script itself is not visible, so its behaviour is unverified.
debug: Open the run in the Actions tab. A failure in Install Playwright points to a version or browser download problem. A failure in Capture points to the script. The message No changes is a normal result, not an error. If the push is rejected, check branch protection or a newer commit on the same branch.
